fields.meta_description: Build a website feedback survey that rates help articles, asks visitors why they came, and posts problem reports to Slack. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Website Feedback Survey That Shows What to Fix
fields.hero_description: Build a website feedback survey that asks visitors one question per screen and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts in Your Feedback Survey
fields.features_subheading: Describe your site and the pages you want feedback on. Emergent builds each part below, and a second prompt changes any of it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions for each kind of page

Name the pages you want rated, such as help articles, pricing, or checkout. Emergent writes the questions for each one, and a follow-up prompt changes any wording before launch.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer in a database you own

Each answer lands as a row in a database you own, beside the page it rates and the date. Filter by page to see which help article or pricing page draws the most complaints.
fields.feature_3:
Problem reports posted to Slack

Problem reports reach the web team through Slack or email alerts, under a rule you set, such as 3 reports naming one page in a day. Single reports wait in the table for review.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Visitors on a phone see one question per screen, with a large tap target for each answer. The same survey works on a laptop, and Emergent puts no cap on how many visitors answer.
fields.feature_5:
Answers sent to the tools you use

Send answers on to your help desk, CRM, or analytics tool through its API. A support lead can open a ticket from a complaint without copying text out of the survey by hand.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Host the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it with your site.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Website Feedback Surveys at Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Import contacts fails 97 readers when one step is missing

Ledgerwick ends every help article with a single question: did this article answer your question? Over 30 days, Import contacts draws 148 answers and 97 say no, the worst of 6 articles. The comments describe the same gap: the article never says how to match the email column.
fields.tab_content_2:
Wholesale buyers quit before reaching the price list

For 14 days, Pinfold Baking Supply asks every visitor what they came to do, and whether they did it. Of 312 who answer, 58 are wholesale buyers, and only 14 of them did. Home bakers finished at 152 of 171. The wholesale comments say the price list sits behind a login.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three reports on one page post to #web-fixes

Oxbury Public Library puts a Report a problem link in the footer of every page. The form asks which page and what went wrong. When 3 reports name the same page within 24 hours, the app posts in the #web-fixes Slack channel. This morning, 4 reports on the room booking page said the form would not submit.
fields.tab_content_4:
After the relaunch, phone visitors find the booking link

Hartsell Family Dental asks phone visitors one question per screen, starting with: can you see how to book? Before the relaunch, 38 of 90 said yes. The new site puts the booking link at the top of every page, and after the relaunch 71 of 88 said yes.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Website Feedback Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a website feedback survey that tells you which page to fix first, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the yes or no question first
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the one page decision this survey should settle, such as which help articles to rewrite or where the booking link goes. Write it at the top of your prompt. A question that cannot change that decision comes out before launch.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with a question that takes one tap: did this page give you what you came for? A yes or no draws the most answers. Add one open comment box after a no, where the visitor names what was missing.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask why the visitor came before you ask how it went. Offer four or five reasons drawn from your own analytics, plus an Other box. A low score then splits by purpose, and you know which group the page failed.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Place the link where the question makes sense: under each help article, on the order confirmation page, or in the footer as Report a problem. Keep it off the first screen of a landing page, where it competes with the page's own goal.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide who hears about a problem
fields.howto_step_5_des: Set a rule for when a problem reaches a person, such as 3 reports on one page within 24 hours. Then name the Slack channel or the person who gets the alert. Everything below the rule waits in the table.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Test the survey on a phone before any visitor sees it. Answer every question, leave the comment box empty once, and submit a no. Check that each answer lands in the table with the right page beside it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the answers on a schedule
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the answers on a fixed schedule, weekly for a busy site and monthly for a small one. Sort pages by the share of no answers, fix the worst one, then compare its next round with the last.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions to ask in a website feedback survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions to ask in a website feedback survey?

prov.original: What are some good questions to ask in a website feedback survey?

faq_plan.a: Ask questions tied to one page and one task. Did this page answer your question? What did you come here to do today, and did you do it? Was anything broken, slow, or hard to find? Did the page work on your phone? Close with one open box: what is the first thing to change?

faq_plan.q: How do I create a website feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the survey to Emergent's AI survey builder in a prompt: the pages it covers, the questions on each, and who gets an alert when a visitor reports a problem. Emergent builds the survey, its logic, and the database behind it, and you can change any part by prompting again. Link it from the pages it rates.

faq_plan.q: What should a website feedback survey template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with a yes or no question on whether the page did its job, then ask why the visitor came, then offer an open box for what was missing. Record the page being rated with every answer, so results sort by page. Keep the whole template to 5 questions or fewer.

faq_plan.q: What are some website feedback survey examples for different kinds of pages?
faq_plan.a: A help article asks whether it answered the reader's question. A pricing page asks what is still unclear about the plans. An order confirmation page asks how checkout went. Feedback on the product or service itself, not the site, belongs in a customer feedback survey sent after purchase.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a website feedback survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep a survey shown on a page to 3 questions or fewer, because the visitor came to do something else. Save longer surveys of 8 to 10 questions for an email to people who already finished a purchase or a sign-up. Emergent sets no response cap on either one.

faq_plan.q: Where should a website feedback survey appear on the page?
faq_plan.a: Put it next to the moment it asks about. A helpfulness question sits at the end of the article, a checkout question on the order confirmation page, and a link to report a problem in the site footer. Skip the pop-up on arrival: the visitor has not seen the page yet.

faq_plan.q: Should website feedback surveys ask what visitors think of the brand?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep them on the site itself: whether a page worked, loaded, and made sense. Questions on how people see the company and its reputation fit a brand perception survey, sent to customers and non-customers alike, where the answers are not tied to a single page.

faq_plan.q: Should a website feedback survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes, make it anonymous by default, since a page rating needs no name. Add an optional email field for visitors who want a reply, and say beside it that the address is used only to answer them. With Emergent, the responses live in a database you own, so that promise is yours to keep.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more visitors to answer a website feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Ask less, and ask at the moment it applies. Open with a one-tap yes or no at the end of the page, and show the comment box only after a no. Show the survey once per visitor. On a phone, keep each question on its own screen.

faq_plan.q: Can a website feedback survey ask how visitors found the site?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add one multiple-choice question, where did you first hear of this site, with options such as search, a friend, social media, and an ad. It shows which channels send visitors. To measure how many people in your market know the brand at all, run a brand awareness survey instead.

They list questions; none shows what a site team does with the answers. This page shows four website feedback surveys that each end in a fix: a help center ranking articles by how many readers say no, a store splitting visits by purpose, a library whose problem reports post to Slack, and a dental practice asking the same booking question before and after a relaunch. The FAQ covers questions, templates, examples, length, placement, anonymity and response rates as plain advice.
